title: How to come up with a consumer startup idea: 5 strategies from 50 winning companies
summary: Lenny studied how 50+ top consumer companies (Airbnb, Uber, Instagram, Coinbase and more) found their ideas. Nearly all came from paying attention: to your own problems, your curiosity, what's already working, paradigm shifts, or brainstorming with friends. He also lists traits of good ideas and what to do first once you have one.

principles.text: Winning consumer ideas come from paying attention, and the largest share come from solving your own problem.
principles.quote: there are only five common strategies for coming up with a great startup idea—**all rooted in paying attention**

principles.text: Don't rely on forced ideation; most big consumer ideas emerged organically rather than from sitting down to brainstorm.
principles.quote: Less than a third of founders were actively ideating** a startup idea when they came up with their big idea. In other words, most startup ideas emerged organically.

principles.text: Launch what excites you now; if one element unexpectedly works, double down on it because it may be the bigger idea.
principles.quote: it should motivate you to launch whatever it is you’re currently most excited about—because even if the idea doesn’t work, it may lead you to the bigger idea.

principles.text: Good ideas come from founders' unique insight and gut instinct, not early user research, and often sound trivial or crazy at first.
principles.quote: rarely is user research a big factor in the early ideating. Most ideas emerged out of the founders’ experience, vision, and gut instincts.

principles.text: A strong idea combines founder obsession, a quick prototype with the skills to build it, unique insight, and simplicity.
principles.quote: Every product we’ve looked at can be explained in a sentence or two.

principles.text: Once you have an idea, prototype it cheaply and quickly to validate it, then talk to potential customers to refine it.
principles.quote: Prototype it cheaply and quickly to validate the idea
